									203 text There is a stronger precedent than a molecular instruction signal. McTernan, De Bo and Leigh constructed a rotaxane in which an aldehyde-bearing growing chain reacts with successive ylide barriers. A Wittig reaction  forms the new carbon–carbon bond, removes the barrier and leaves a new terminal aldehyde . The chemical product therefore owns the ability to proceed. Their four-addition construction required five days and gave 21% isolated product, with hydrolysis/deletion and alkene-isomer limitations. It did not establish a renewed twenty-step factory.
